definition: General Architecture for Text Engineering (GATE) is a Java suite of natural language processing (NLP) tools for man tasks, including information extraction in many languages.
details: It is now used worldwide by a wide community of scientists, companies, teachers and students. It was originally developed at the University of Sheffield beginning in 1995. As of May 28, 2011, 881 people are on the gate-users mailing list at SourceForge.net, and 111,932 downloads from SourceForge are recorded since the project moved to SourceForge in 2005. The paper "GATE: A framework and graphical development environment for robust NLP tools and applications" has received over 2000 citations since publication (according to Google Scholar). Books covering the use of GATE, in addition to the GATE User Guide, include "Building Search Applications: Lucene, LingPipe, and Gate", by Manu Konchady, and "Introduction to Linguistic Annotation and Text Analytics", by Graham Wilcock. GATE community and research has been involved in several European research projects including: Transitioning Applications to Ontologies, SEKT, NeOn, Media-Campaign, Musing, Service-Finder, LIRICS and KnowledgeWeb.

explainer.lead: General Architecture for Text Engineering, or GATE, is a Java-based suite for building and running natural language processing work, including information extraction in many languages. It gives researchers, companies, teachers, and students a shared environment rather than requiring each text-processing task to start from scratch.

tiers.eli5: GATE is like a workbench filled with tools for reading and sorting information in text. Instead of making every tool yourself, you can use the workbench to help find useful information in documents written in different languages.
tiers.practitioner: GATE is applied as a Java NLP suite, with a framework and graphical development environment for text-processing tools and applications. A typical use is information extraction across documents and languages, using GATE as the shared development and processing environment.
tiers.paperLevel: GATE is formally a general architecture for text engineering: a Java suite and framework for robust NLP tools and applications, supporting tasks such as multilingual information extraction. Development began at the University of Sheffield in 1995, and the associated framework paper is "GATE: A framework and graphical development environment for robust NLP tools and applications."

explainer.example: A researcher with documents in several languages uses GATE to run information-extraction tools in one environment, rather than creating a separate processing system for each language.

explainer.intuition: GATE provides a common workbench for language-processing tasks, so tools and applications can be developed within one architecture. Its scope includes information extraction across many languages.
howItWorks: Start with text that needs language processing.
Use GATE's Java-based NLP tools within its framework and graphical development environment.
Apply the tools to the chosen task, such as information extraction.
Use the resulting processed text or extracted information in an NLP application.
explainer.whyItMatters: A shared architecture makes NLP tools and applications easier to develop and reuse across tasks and languages. GATE's international community and its use in research projects show its role as common infrastructure for text engineering.
misconceptions: GATE is not a single NLP algorithm; it is a suite and framework for tools and applications.
It is not restricted to English or one language; its tasks include information extraction in many languages.
